transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has just been all over the place lately. Um, some weeks I barely even touch my dinner. But then other nights... I'll just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets long after everyone else has gone to bed. It's just been really inconsistent, so I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone.
When you eat like that late at night, does it feel hard to stop or control how much you’re eating?
No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm out of control or anything. It's just... I'm up, and I'm hungry, so I eat. I could stop if I wanted to, I just usually don't want to until I'm full.
When you eat late at night, is it usually after you’ve woken up from sleep?
No, I usually haven't gone to sleep yet. I just stay up late, and since I'm awake, I end up snacking. It's not like I'm waking up in the middle of the night to eat.
Are you very worried about your weight or body shape?

No, not really. I mean, I notice if my clothes fit a little differently, but it's not something I stress over. I'm just more annoyed by how unpredictable my appetite has been, rather than worrying about how I look.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah, I have. I go through these stretches where... well, the whole house just feels gray and heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table feeling completely empty, even though nothing terrible has actually happened that day.
When you feel that heavy, empty mood, do you lose interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I do. Things I used to really look forward to just... start feeling like chores. Like my book club, or cooking, going to galleries, even tending the rose beds. I just keep putting them off because I completely lose the interest to do them when I'm in that headspace.
When your mood gets that heavy and empty, do you lose your appetite?

Well, it's actually been all over the place. Honestly, that's what finally pushed me to come in. Some weeks, yeah, I lose it and I barely touch my dinner. But then... other nights, I'll just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets long after everyone else has gone to bed. So it's not just losing my appetite, it really just goes back and forth.
When you get into that heavy, empty mood, does it last most of the day?

Yeah, it does. Like I was saying before about the house feeling so gray and just sitting at the table feeling empty... that isn't just for an hour or two. When I get into those stretches, that heavy feeling usually settles in and lasts for the majority of the day, even when absolutely nothing bad has happened to trigger it.
When these heavy, empty stretches happen, do they last for at least two weeks at a time?

I don't think so. I mean, I haven't really kept track on a calendar or anything, but... I don't think it's ever been two whole weeks straight. It definitely drags on for a few days at a time, but I haven't noticed it lasting quite that long.
Did these heavy, empty stretches start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?
No, not really. I mean, I've tried to think back and see if there was some big trigger, but... nothing stands out. It just kind of happens on its own, without any real reason that I can point to.
During those stretches, do you find yourself feeling very anxious or worried?

No, I wouldn't really say that. It's not so much about worrying or feeling anxious. It's just... like I said, mostly just feeling heavy and empty. I don't really get worked up or nervous during those times, it's just more of a blankness.
During those heavy, empty stretches, do you have trouble sleeping?
No, my sleep is usually pretty normal then. I might sleep a little more than usual just because I don't feel like getting up, but I don't have trouble falling asleep or anything.
During those heavy, empty stretches, do you feel unusually tired or low on energy?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel completely exhausted or anything. It's more just... a lack of motivation, I guess? Like, I physically have the energy, but I just don't have the drive to do much of anything. It's not like a deep, physical tiredness.
During those heavy, empty stretches, do you find yourself feeling worthless or overly guilty?

Yes, I do actually. I get really stuck on things. I can spend hours just replaying small mistakes in my head... like if I bought an expensive tube of pigment for painting, or if I just snapped at my spouse. I'll just dwell on it and start to feel like I've ruined the whole household because of that one little thing.
During those heavy, empty stretches, do you have trouble concentrating or making decisions?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean... I can still focus on things if I need to. Like, if I'm reading a book or deciding what to make for dinner, my mind works fine. I don't get that foggy feeling where you can't think straight. So, no, my concentration and decision-making are pretty normal.
During those heavy, empty stretches, have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

Well... I haven't made any sort of plan to actually hurt myself. I wouldn't do that. But, um, on the worst nights... I do sometimes think it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. It's just a thought that crosses my mind when the feeling gets really heavy.
When you have those late-night eating episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

No, I don't really do that. I mean... I don't have episodes where I eat a huge amount of food all at once. If I'm up late and get hungry, I might just grab a normal snack, like a piece of toast or something. But it's definitely not an unusually large amount of food in a short time.
During those heavy, empty stretches, do other people notice that you’re moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?
No, nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I don't think I move or talk any slower than I usually do, even when I'm feeling really down. I just kind of keep to my normal pace.
